newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria raises yields on T-bills for individuals. [CORRECTED 14:23 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria raises yields on T-bills for individuals. [CORRECTED 14:23 GMT]

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Ministry said on Wednesday it had decided to offer higher yields on special T-bill issues aimed at companies and individuals.

"We have decided to raise the yield on three-month, six-month and one-year T-bills that we offer to companies and individuals," said Plamen Oresharski, head of the State Treasury and Debt department in the Finance Ministry.
The yield of three-month T-bills will be set at the Bulgarian National Bank's (BNB) central interest rate (CIR), Oresharski said. The new yields come in force from next Monday.
The CIR is currently set at 108 percent annually. (Corrects the central interest figure).
The coupon of the six-month T-bills will be CIR + 1/7 CIR or 123.4 percent, and of the one-year ones - CIR + 1/2 CIR or 162 percent, said Oresharski.
The current yield of the three-month, six-month and one-year T-bills is set at respetively CIR-15 or 93 percent, CIR-3 or 105 percent and CIR+25 or 133 percent.

The increase in the yield of the special issues for companies and individuals comes a couple of weeks after the State Savings Bank and some other commercial bank raised the interest rates on their deposits.
"The yield on special issues was raised to harmonise it with the much higher yield offered on T-paper investments by financial institutions," another Finance Ministry official told Reuters.
Higher yields are offered to compensate the erosion of lev-denominated investments by quickening inflation and the weakening lev, said the official.
A 56-day discount T-bill issue was sold on Monday yielding record high 289.54 percent annually, the BNB said.
On Tuesday Oresharski said that the Finance Ministry planned to cover principal and maturity payments on government domestic debt through new regular issues of treasury paper.
